slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1904; white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1904 returns.

slices.label: Black Southerners
slices.source: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1904; Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement was near complete across the region (Alabama 1901, Virginia 1902 and Texas's 1902 poll tax had joined Mississippi, South Carolina, Louisiana and North Carolina); the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.

south-white.name: Anna Reed
south-white.quote: I wish I could have a say in this, but the law doesn't allow women to vote here. My husband will cast our ballot tomorrow.
south-white.controlQuote: I wish I could have a say in this, but the law doesn't allow women to vote here. My husband will cast our ballot tomorrow.

women.name: Ruth Robinson
women.quote: I can't vote—women don't have that right here. My husband will handle it tomorrow.

men.name: Ernest Reed
men.quote: The tariff keeps our mills running and our wages steady, though I wonder if Parker might have a point about the trusts getting too big. Still, I'll likely back the administration's man tomorrow.
